ca3.description: Ten years after the Government of Canada officially adopted the term "Indigenous" instead of "Aboriginal," discussions persist on what terms best describe First Nations, Inuit and Métis.

ca3.title: Convicted drug trafficker to keep Halifax-area lakeside home, but will pay $240K fine
ca3.description: Gary (Boo) Boudreau, who was targeted by a major cocaine and cannabis investigation, will not lose the million-dollar lakeside home he built partly on the proceeds of crime, but has instead been ordered to pay a $240,000 fine for the portion linked to his illegal profits.

ca3.title: Canadians ready to play ball as 1st season of Women's Pro Baseball League gets underway
ca3.description: Nearly a dozen Canadian athletes are going to be part of the chase to be the first-ever champions of the Women's Pro Baseball League, which begins its inaugural season in the United States on Saturday.

ca3.title: 2 teens charged with 2nd-degree murder of woman in Prince Albert, Sask.
ca3.description: Two teenagers have been charged with second-degree murder after 27-year-old Daina Gauthier was fatally stabbed on Thursday in Prince Albert.

ca3.title: One of Calgary's most decorated Second World War veterans dies at 101
ca3.description: Navy Capt. William (Bill) Wilson enlisted in the Royal Canadian Navy in 1942, serving aboard HMCS Ottawa as a seaman gunner during the latter stages of the Battle of the Atlantic and taking part in the D-Day landings at Normandy.

ca3.title: Kayaker on St. John River makes a pair of grim discoveries
ca3.description: ​Melissa Lavigne has done a lot of kayaking on the St. John River, but on a recent paddle, she came across something new: a headstone and grave marker for two long-dead Fredericton men.

ca3.title: Winnipeg man pleads guilty to advocating genocide and wilfully promoting hatred in social media posts
ca3.description: A Winnipeg man who self-identified as being "extremely racist" in posts he made on social media has pleaded guilty to advocating genocide and wilfully promoting hatred against Muslims and Jews.

ca3.title: Saskatoon fire crews searching river after reports of missing person, dog
ca3.description: Reports of a person and dog in the river came in at 11:50 a.m. CST on Friday, said Saskatoon fire chief Doug Wegren.

ca3.title: Community gathers to mourn 11-year-old Calgary boy after end of near 2-week search
ca3.description: A crowd of people attended one of several gatherings Thursday evening for Parker, the 11-year-old Calgary boy who went missing earlier this month and was confirmed dead earlier that day.

ca3.title: Feds approve Crawford Nickel Project in Ontario, promising it'll create 5,000 jobs during build
ca3.description: The federal government has approved the Crawford Nickel Project in Northern Ontario saying the mine will draw in $5 billion in investment and create 5,000 jobs during its construction and another 1,300 jobs for operation.

ca3.title: Permits issued for Alberta coal mine expansion despite environmental opposition
ca3.description: A sprawling expansion of a massive thermal coal mine near Hinton, Alta., has been approved by Alberta’s provincial regulator, clearing the way for the operator to extend the life of the project well into the next decade.
